## 5. Functional Requirements

> **Testing strategy**: All requirements verified via automated tests (unit, integration, UI) targeting 90%+ coverage unless otherwise specified. Document a verification method only for non-test approaches (analysis, inspection, demonstration).

Functional requirements define WHAT the platform must do. Each is a checkbox with a priority marker `p1`-`p9` (assigned by business impact). Platform FRs describe host-app and shared-kernel capabilities — capabilities owned by a single MiniApp belong in that MiniApp's PRD.

## 6. Non-Functional Requirements

> **NFR framing**: State NFRs as business-level quality expectations — user/business outcomes, SLAs, and measurable targets (e.g., "cold start to first interactive screen under 3s at p95 on a mid-tier device"). Do NOT specify technical implementation (caching strategy, technology stack, component tuning) — those belong in DESIGN/ADR.

Platform NFRs are the project-wide defaults. MiniApps inherit them and document only stricter or excluded cases.

## Appendix: ID Reference

`{hierarchy-prefix}` is the dot-free hierarchy path of the platform node as registered in `artifacts.toml` — for this platform it is `superapp`.

| ID Pattern | Example | Purpose |
|------------|---------|---------|
| `cpt-{hierarchy-prefix}-prd` | `cpt-superapp-prd` | Platform PRD anchor |
| `cpt-{hierarchy-prefix}-actor-{slug}` | `cpt-superapp-actor-student` | Actor (defined here, referenced everywhere) |
| `cpt-{hierarchy-prefix}-fr-{slug}` | `cpt-superapp-fr-single-sign-on` | Functional requirement |
| `cpt-{hierarchy-prefix}-nfr-{slug}` | `cpt-superapp-nfr-cold-start` | Non-functional requirement |
| `cpt-{hierarchy-prefix}-interface-{slug}` | `cpt-superapp-interface-shared-kernel` | Public interface |
| `cpt-{hierarchy-prefix}-contract-{slug}` | `cpt-superapp-contract-push-delivery` | Integration contract |
| `cpt-{hierarchy-prefix}-usecase-{slug}` | `cpt-superapp-usecase-first-launch` | Use case |
